nodes.description: Private constant bytes32 guard value, keccak256("guard.bytes32"), stored in contract storage at construction time.
Address of external library/contract whose code is executed via delegatecall inside batchLogs.
bytes32 guard flag initialised to GUARD_VALUE in the constructor and compared against GUARD_VALUE in batchLogs.
Public mapping(address => UnlockSchedule[]) holding unlock schedules; readable externally.
Constructor that stores the external gatedLogBatcherLib address and sets guard to GUARD_VALUE.
Public unrestricted function that requires guard != GUARD_VALUE then delegatecalls the external library with attacker-supplied logs calldata.
Caller of the public batchLogs function; no access control restricts who may invoke it.
Low-level delegatecall to gatedLogBatcherLib with ABI-encoded multiSend(bytes) data, executing untrusted external code in this contract's storage context.
Constructor parameter supplying the address stored in gatedLogBatcherLib.
Arbitrary bytes payload supplied by the caller and forwarded as calldata to the delegatecall target.
Hash emitted in the BatchLogs event after the delegatecall returns.
Local bool returned by the low-level delegatecall (unused, no revert on failure).
Local bytes returned by the low-level delegatecall (unused).

edges.reason: Constructor writes the supplied library address into the gatedLogBatcherLib state variable.
Constructor initialises the guard state variable to GUARD_VALUE.
Constructor reads the constant GUARD_VALUE to assign guard.
batchLogs is public and callable by any msg.sender; no owner/permission check guards entry.
batchLogs reads the guard state variable in its require(guard != GUARD_VALUE) check.
batchLogs compares guard against the constant GUARD_VALUE.
batchLogs unconditionally executes the delegatecall unsafe operation after the guard check.
Target address of the delegatecall is the gatedLogBatcherLib state variable.
Caller-controlled logs bytes are ABI-encoded and passed as calldata to the delegatecall.
contentHash parameter flows into the BatchLogs event emitted by batchLogs.
delegatecall executes external code in this contract's context, allowing the callee to re-enter batchLogs before the BatchLogs event completes.
Success flag of the delegatecall is captured in the local success variable.
Return data of the delegatecall is captured in the local data variable.
unlockSchedules shares contract storage with the delegatecall, so delegated code can arbitrarily overwrite it.

normalization_plan.reason: Constructor parameter is only used to set the gatedLogBatcherLib state variable, so it can be folded into the constructor node.
Caller-supplied logs bytes are consumed directly as calldata by the delegatecall unsafe operation and carry no independent identity.
Emitting contentHash is an internal effect of batchLogs and the parameter has no standalone semantic role.
Local success flag only reflects the delegatecall outcome and is never used in any branch, so it can be merged into its enclosing function.
Local return-data buffer is unused and only an artifact of the low-level delegatecall inside batchLogs.
